project-01.main_title: Building an AI-powered visa document generator to help travellers across the world.
project-01.intro_part1: The idea behind **visadocs.ai** began long before I ever considered building it, back when I was constantly frustrated by the paperwork involved in visa applications — both for myself and when helping my relatives.
project-01.intro_part2: I built the platform with a simple goal: to **streamline and simplify the visa application process.** Since requirements vary widely from one country to another, I decided to start with **travel itineraries**, as they are one of the most commonly required documents in visa applications.
project-01.intro_part3: Behind the scenes, it runs on a modern **React + Cloudflare stack**, integrates securely with **Stripe for payments**, and supports multilingual PDF generation. All generated PDFs are carefully **designed to meet typical embassy standards.**
project-01.specs_tools: Figma, OpenAI, Github, Git, Cloudflare, Brevo, EmailJS
project-01.specs_stack: React+Vite, Cloudflare, OpenAI API, Google Places API, Stripe Payments
project-01.objective_title: Offering a way to generate quality PDF travel itineraries in less than 2 minutes.
project-01.objective_intro: With many travel and visa-consultancy agencies offering tailored services, the idea was to build a **SaaS platform** which would be:

features.title: Product centred
features.content: A tool to simplify a complex part of the visa process.

features.title: Fast
features.content: Reducing time and stress during the visa demand process.

features.title: Quality focused
features.content: Serving top-tier PDFs that meet embassy format standards.

features.title: Global
features.content: Multi-language export to help users worldwide.

features.title: Single usage
features.content: You don’t apply for a visa every day, so no account is needed.

features.title: Affordable
features.content: A one-time, low-cost service to keep visa demand affordable.

project-01.process_title: POC → Low-fi design → Prototype & Tests → High-fi design → Final build
project-01.challenge_title: Where AI fell short. And why custom logic was needed.

challenge.intro_part1: When I started working on **visadocs.ai**, the idea was pretty clear in my mind. I would **leverage the power of AI to translate data from my front-end’s form into a well-constructed table.**
challenge.intro_part2: That table would feature, for each day of the travel itinerary **all the key information necessary**, and would include accurate data (no placeholder values).
challenge.blk1_part1: After some tests, I realised that itineraries **couldn’t be exported as PDFs**, nor could they **include real or accurate location data for the cities and hotels.**
challenge.blk1_part2: **Why?** When calling an AI model API directly, only the model’s “basic” reasoning layer is available. Anything more advanced **require using external APIs and libraries.**
challenge.blk2_part1: **Building the logic came piece by piece:** Integrating powerful APIs like Google Places API and REST API or using libraries like pdf-lib to turn complex JSON into clean, readable PDFs, and manually refining itineraries for multilingual use.
challenge.blk2_part2: The logic would have to be more complex and fragmented but also **more scalable and robust.**
challenge.outro_small: After the countless hours spent, I realised
challenge.outro_main: I took full ownership of the build, growing my skills with every step.

project-01.delivery_title: A scalable and robust system for quickly generating travel itineraries

project-02.main_title: Creating a new identity and a fresh website for a visa consultancy agency.
project-02.intro_part1: In 2024, I returned to hands-on product design work after a period exploring a different craft. This project marked **my re-entry into digital product work**, where I partnered with **JMR Visa Services** to redesign their digital presence.
project-02.intro_part2: This project focused on redesigning the online presence of **JMR Visa Services** to increase trust and improve lead conversion. The challenge was to improve the existing website into a **clear and trustworthy experience** through improved information architecture, refreshed branding, and streamlined contact flows.
project-02.intro_part3: **I owned the project end to end**, from product strategy and UX to visual design, front-end development (React + Tailwind), and Cloudflare-based hosting and deployment.

project-03.main_title: Leading the design of a feature facilitating conversations during live events.
project-03.intro_part1: The **Chat feature** was **born from a global shift in the events and conference landscape** during the 2020 **COVID-19** outbreak. Physical events like conferences and town halls drastically declined, while **digital events and online meetings rapidly expanded.**
project-03.intro_part2: As a result, **many of Pigeonhole Live’s core features had to be adapted**, as they were originally built for in-person experiences. During this period, much of my focus was on **product improvements and third-party integrations** with platforms such as Zoom, MS Teams or Webex.
project-03.intro_part3: The lack of physical presence and live audience feedback meant that **engagement was harder to grasp for event organisers** (Pigeonhole Live’s primary users). This gap led to the creation of the **Chat feature**, providing audiences with **a way to connect with both speakers and fellow attendees during digital and hybrid events.**
